t: You're looking at the UCL Institute of Archaeology, housed in a 1950s building on the north side of Gordon Square in Bloomsbury. It's one of the largest centres in the world for the study of archaeology, cultural heritage and museum studies, with over a hundred staff and six hundred students. It joined University College London in 1986. It was founded by Mortimer Wheeler and his wife Tessa Wheeler. Mortimer directed the National Museum of Wales and the London Museum. Tessa was a South Africa-born archaeologist who helped improve excavation techniques and set up major British archaeological institutions.
